correctness.rationale: De Cataldo's product formula gives \(F(q)=\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{-e}\). Formal logarithmic differentiation yields \(qF'(q)=eF(q)\sum_{j\ge1}\sigma_1(j)q^j\), hence \(n a_n=e\sum_{j=1}^n\sigma_1(j)a_{n-j}\). Therefore \(e\mid n a_n\), and cancelling \(\gcd(|e|,n)\) gives \(|e|/\gcd(|e|,n)\mid a_n\). The \(e=0\) case follows from \(F=1\). The argument also works for negative Euler characteristic because it is an identity of formal power series. The bundled finite expansion is consistent but is not needed for the proof.
risks: The statement is only about total compactly supported Euler characteristic; it says nothing about refined Betti/Hodge data.
The phrase 'uniformly sharp' is only justified in the across-all-n sense by n=1; it is not pointwise sharp for every fixed n.
